nodes.name: Every 5 minutes
nodes.notes: Five minutes, matching the liveness timeout in api/_lib/health.ts. Worst-case detection is therefore about ten minutes, which is the trade for an alert that stays quiet enough to be believed.

nodes.name: Load config
nodes.notes: alwaysOutputData: without it, an empty config table emits no items, the downstream 'Assess' node never runs, and the monitor ends quietly. A missing config row is itself a degraded state.

nodes.name: Check health
nodes.notes: neverError so a 503 — which is the whole point of this workflow — is read rather than thrown. onError continues on network-level failures too (DNS, connection refused): those must reach the Assess node and be classified degraded, not stop the workflow before it can alert. /api/health needs no secret: it returns three ages and a count, and a health check that needs a credential is one nobody wires up.

nodes.name: Notify
nodes.notes: Slack-shaped {text}, which most incoming-webhook services accept. onError continues on purpose: an unset or broken webhook must not swallow the failure below it — losing the alert channel is not the same as delivery being fine.

nodes.name: Raise
nodes.notes: Second, independent channel. Failing the execution puts the outage in n8n's own execution list and failure rate, so the alert survives a webhook that was never configured, was revoked, or points at a channel nobody reads.
